ev.q: CDC analyzed injury mortality data by Indian Health Service (IHS) administrative area and by race/ethnicity.
AI/AN rates for all injuries combined were two times greater than overall U.S. rates (49.4 versus 24.0, respectively)
During 1989--1998, injury death rates declined for AI/ANs from all motor-vehicle crashes (14%)
Firearms (52%) and hanging (37%) were the leading methods of suicide for AI/AN youth.
Compared with blacks and whites, AI/AN children and youth had the highest injury-death rates
All rates were age-adjusted by using the 2000 U.S. standard population.
Mortality data were obtained from CDC's National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS)
During 1989--1998, injury death rates declined for AI/ANs from all motor-vehicle crashes (14%)

methods_quotes.q: All rates were age-adjusted by using the 2000 U.S. standard population.
AI/AN rates were calculated by using the IHS service population for 1989--1998
Black, white, and overall U.S. death rates were calculated by using CDC's Web-Based Injury Statistics Query and Reporting System
Rates are based on <20 deaths and should be interpreted with caution.
